dod_intent_evidence: Five Phase II SBIR/STTR/AFWERX/SpaceWERX awards in 18 months plus a $4M U.S. Space Force TACFI contract (May 2026) to demonstrate GPS-independent PNT (News section) — genuine, active DoD motion, still pre-fielding ('2027 Target for Initial Rollout').
score_evidence: "TrustPoint intends to lead that revolution with our microsatellite based commercial infrastructure and innovative positioning and timing services" → lab_language_intensity (disruption/vision language, no operational framing)

"Air, Marine, Mounted and Dismounted Applications for the DoD and IC" is the only warfighter-adjacent phrase in ~1339 words of own language — no DDIL, ATO/RMF, CMMC, ITAR, or STIG term appears anywhere → deployment_awareness_absence
Same sector-label line is the closest the site gets to operator language; no mention of training, CONOPS, or field feedback from actual warfighters → operator_absence

Open roles (Blitz): Senior VHDL Digital Communications Engineer, Embedded Software Engineer x2, Electrical and RF Engineer x2, Satellite Operations Engineer, Ground Station Lead x3 → hiring_profile_skew (satellite/RF/embedded engineering-heavy; zero field, compliance, or ISSO roles)

"TrustPoint Accelerates Defense-Grade, GPS-Independent PNT with Fifth Phase II SBIR Award in 18 Months" (Feb 2026) and "TrustPoint Sets 2027 Target for Initial Rollout of LEO-Based Navigation Services" (Dec 2025) → stage_pressure (multiple parallel funded efforts racing toward a hard rollout deadline)

blind_spots.blind_spot: Anti-jam/anti-spoof resilience is marketed in pure commercial-disruption language, with no mention of M-Code, MGUE, or NAVWAR interoperability standards that DoD PNT programs actually require to integrate with fielded receivers.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A warfighter-grade PNT alternative that doesn't speak the M-Code/MGUE integration language the Army and Air Force already standardized on means the DoD customer has to build an entirely new integration path before a single unit reaches a soldier.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's public identity and hiring (RF/embedded/ground-station engineers) is built for the commercial GNSS market first, DoD/IC listed as one of four target sectors alongside automotive and critical infrastructure.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "TrustPoint aims to provide this diversity and resilience" with zero mention of M-Code, MGUE, or NAVWAR anywhere on the site

blind_spots.blind_spot: The entire PNT solution depends on a LEO satellite constellation and continuous downlink to ground stations — the same jamming/spoofing threat TrustPoint claims to solve for GPS could equally deny the uplink/downlink to their own commercial constellation, and this failure mode is never addressed.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A dismounted or mounted warfighter in a DDIL environment needs PNT to keep working when comms are denied, not just when GPS specifically is denied — swapping one satellite dependency for another doesn't solve the contested-environment problem.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The pitch is framed around GPS resilience specifically, not the broader DDIL threat model DoD operational users actually face.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "With new threats on the rise globally, it is even more important to complement the heritage GPS... to enhance resiliency, accuracy, and security against jamming and spoofing" — no mention of what happens if their own LEO downlink is jammed

blind_spots.blind_spot: No SWaP-C discussion anywhere for the actual user-carried receiver/terminal — all public language describes the satellite-side infrastructure and abstract commercial applications (autonomous cars, aviation, critical infrastructure), never the physical form factor a dismounted soldier would carry.
blind_spots.operator_reality: TRX Systems' DAPS II (a comparable PNT competitor) leads with exact dimensions, weight, MIL-STD-810G rating, and battery-swap logistics — the absence of any of that in TrustPoint's public materials signals the user-terminal engineering hasn't caught up to the constellation narrative.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team and hiring (VHDL, RF, ground-station, satellite ops) are concentrated on the space segment, not the user-terminal/field-hardware segment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "microsatellite based commercial infrastructure and innovative positioning and timing services" — infrastructure-only framing, no terminal hardware described

opener_hook: Your fifth Phase II SBIR in eighteen months (Feb 2026) is racing toward a 2027 LEO-PNT rollout target — what does the dismounted-warfighter terminal look like once the constellation is up?
what_they_do: Commercial LEO satellite constellation delivering GPS-independent/resilient position-navigation-timing (PNT), marketed across commercial (auto, aviation, infrastructure) and DoD/IC national-security sectors.
